close_reason:
Applied option (a) (return VacationResponse directly) plus the bead's optional 'raw variant' suggestion: vacation_response_get now returns VacationResponse (unwrapped from the spec-mandated singleton list), and a new vacation_response_get_envelope method returns the full GetResponse<VacationResponse> envelope for callers that need the 'state' token (e.g. for ifInState guards on vacation_response_set).

vacation_response_get implementation: delegates to vacation_response_get_envelope, then takes the first element of the .list Vec. An empty list — which RFC 8621 §8 declares a spec violation since the singleton always exists per account — is mapped to ClientError::InvalidSession with a description that explains the spec invariant. The bead recommended this exact escape-hatch shape.

README.md method table updated to reflect both signatures. Pre-publish 0.1.x kit, no published consumers, so the API break is invisible. Test in mod tests asserts on the raw GetResponse<VacationResponse> wire-shape deserialize (independent serde oracle) and is unaffected.

Rustdoc cross-references the two methods so callers discovering one find the other naturally.
description:
vacation.rs:28-38

  pub async fn vacation_response_get(&self)
      -> Result<GetResponse<jmap_mail_types::VacationResponse>, ClientError>

The function passes `ids: ["singleton"]` to the wire request (line 33-34). RFC 8621 §8 says the VacationResponse object is a per-account SINGLETON with id="singleton". The module docstring (line 4-5) acknowledges this:

  "VacationResponse is a singleton object per account (RFC 8621 §8). Its `id`
   is always `"singleton"`. `VacationResponse/get` ignores the `ids` argument
   and always returns the single object"

Yet the return type is GetResponse<VacationResponse>, which contains a Vec<VacationResponse>. The caller has to:

  let resp = sc.vacation_response_get().await?;
  let v = resp.list.first().ok_or(...)?;

…where the spec promises resp.list.len() == 1.

Defensive-code-forcing: every caller writes the same `.first()` boilerplate. The type signature does not encode the spec's singleton guarantee.

Recommendation: change the return type to:

  pub async fn vacation_response_get(&self)
      -> Result<VacationResponse, ClientError>

with extraction logic in the method body. Optionally, keep a "raw" variant for callers who need access to old_state / new_state / notFound (though notFound is essentially meaningless for a singleton — either the server has the singleton or doesn't).

Two design choices:

  (a) Return VacationResponse directly. Server-returned empty list = ClientError::InvalidSession or a new ClientError::NotFound. Simplest API, but the empty-list case is rare (server doesn't have a vacation response set? RFC 8621 §8 implies one always exists per account, defaulting to isEnabled=false).

  (b) Return Option<VacationResponse> — None signals server returned empty list.

Recommendation: (a). Per RFC 8621 §8 the singleton always exists, so server-returned-empty-list is a protocol violation and ClientError::InvalidSession is the right escape hatch.

Cross-reference: vacation_response_set on line 54-72 returns SetResponse<VacationResponse>. SetResponse from RFC 8620 §5.3 has the same Vec issue but in different form (updated is a HashMap<Id, ...>). Less acute since the caller already knows the id key ("singleton") to look up.

Mark says NO HUMAN — recommendation (a). The wire response from a spec-conformant server WILL always have exactly one entry; if it doesn't, that's a server bug worth surfacing as ClientError.
title: vacation_response_get returns GetResponse<VacationResponse> with Vec for a documented singleton — forces caller to index into list
